memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses then said to Aaron, 'This is what the LORD spoke of when he said: "Among those who approach me I will be proved holy; in the sight of all the people I will be honoured."' Aaron remained silent." - Lev 10:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron remained silent.

Three words, and they carry an ocean. A father has just watched two of his four sons die. Moses speaks about God's holiness. And Aaron says nothing at all.

We should be careful how we read that silence. It is not necessarily agreement, and it is certainly not indifference. It may be shock. It may be a grief too deep for speech. It may be a man submitting to God without understanding Him.

Scripture does not tell us, and that restraint is itself instructive. The Bible does not tidy up Aaron's grief or rush him toward the right feelings.

There are moments in life when there is nothing to say. When the loss is too large, when the explanation does not help, when even true words about God's holiness cannot reach the wound yet.

Job's friends sat with him seven days and no one said a word to him, because they saw how great his suffering was (Job 2:13). That was the best thing they ever did. Everything they said afterwards made it worse.

If you are in a season where you cannot pray in sentences, you are in good company. God is not waiting for you to articulate anything.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there a grief in my life I have never allowed myself to sit with honestly?
2. Am I quick to offer explanations to hurting people when silence might serve better?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You understand what I cannot put into words. Meet me in the silence, and teach me to sit quietly with others who are suffering. Amen.
